newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-SHAAMIT IN TOP FORM AHEAD OF IRISH CHAMPION STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SHAAMIT IN TOP FORM AHEAD OF IRISH CHAMPION STAKES.

text.p: Newmarket trainer William Haggas said on Friday that Epsom Derby winner Shaamit was in top form ahead of the valuable group one Irish Champion Stakes at Leopardstown.
"Everything is in order for Saturday. Shaamit completed his preparations on Thursday and he is in top form," said Haggas.
"The only worry I have at this stage concerns the fact that he is travelling over to Ireland for the race on what is (unlucky) Friday the 13th," he added.
Shaamit, who will be ridden over the 10-furlong (2-km) trip by Michael Hills, is 6-4 favourite with Dublin bookmakers to land Saturday's $241,000 event.
The colt was ridden by Pat Eddery when third last time out behind the more experienced Pentire and Classic Cliche in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot.
Six runners, three trained in Ireland and three in Britain, remained in the field at Friday's final declaration stage.
The British challenge is completed by the Godolphin-trained Tamayaz (7-1) and Paul Kelleway's 8-1 chance Glory of Dancer.
Gary Carter will partner Tamayaz while Glory Of Dancer will be ridden by Frenchman Olivier Peslier who took him to fourth place in the Epsom Derby.

The home team, bidding for a first Irish victory in the race since 1986, is headed by John Oxx-trained Timarida (100-30), the recent winner of a grade one race at at Arlington, and Dermot Weld's Irish Oaks winner Dance Design (7-2).
Timarida, successful in seven of her eight races in 1995, has won races in four countries.
Dance Design represents Weld in place of runaway Irish Derby score Zagreb for whom the Leopardstown going was thought too firm.
The Irish challenge is completed by 10-1 chance Idris, bidding for his seventh win of the year under Kevin Manning, but stepping up in class.
